candidates.rationale: Low spill, queueing, and latency make one-size down a controlled canary candidate; absence of pressure is not proof of SLA safety.
No sustained saturation requiring an increase and no strong evidence for a lower ceiling.
The cost-minimizing auto-stop on measured running idle time, counting the restarts it adds, within the cold-start budget.
Pro is evaluated as an alternate migration experiment for Serverless warehouses. The estimate is pre-canary and compatibility remains a deterministic gate.

assumptions: Current configuration epoch is the decision baseline.
Forward DBU cost uses the deterministic current-epoch run-rate model.
AWS forward cost is modeled from observed current-epoch resource time and the configured regional price registry when available.
DBU cost is priced at the account's list price; negotiated discounts lower real savings in proportion.
AWS cost is priced at on-demand EC2 rates; Spot, Reserved Instances and Savings Plans are not modeled.

recommended_plan.decision_summary: Plan A — Optimize current warehouse type is the deterministic execution path; apply validation gates and regenerate after invalidating changes. Apply the ready no-canary steps (auto_stop_minutes) first; start the warehouse_size canary once the next run shows their new configuration ready (2 settled billed days), so the canary's cost reading is not mixed with their savings.

portfolio_economics.method: Stateful DBU+AWS bundle. Each step changes the evolving cost/resource state. Min-cluster and auto-stop remove remaining cluster-minutes rather than adding standalone savings; migration steps replace the state with a DBU+AWS pre-canary counterfactual.

scenarios.scenario_name: Plan A — Optimize current warehouse type

portfolio_economics.method: Migration candidate lacks a deterministic DBU counterfactual; cost is withheld until required source pricing/resource evidence is available.
